'''Francisc Joel Martínez Vilar''' (born 31 December 1988) is a retired Andorran [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]] and current Head of Football School at [[Inter Club d'Escaldes|Inter d'Escaldes]].<ref name="Soccerway">{{cite news|title=Andorra - Francisco Martínez|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/francisco-martinez/228793/|accessdate=14 December 2018|work=Soccerway}}</ref>

==Club career==
Martínez's senior career began with [[UE Sant Julià]] in 2005, remaining with the [[Primera Divisió]] team until 2006 when the midfielder agreed to join Andorran-based Spanish Tercera Catalana side [[FC Andorra]].<ref name="NFT">{{cite news|title=Joel Martinez - National Football Teams|url=https://www.national-football-teams.com/player/8438/Joel_Martinez.html|accessdate=14 December 2018|work=NFT}}</ref> Martínez spent the [[2007–08 Primera Divisió]] season back with Sant Julià, prior to returning to Spain with FC Andorra for the following campaign.<ref name="NFT"/> This spell with the club lasted five years, with Martínez netting twelve goals in one hundred and twenty-six appearances.<ref name="NFT"/> He rejoined Sant Julià for a third time in 2013, subsequently winning the [[Copa Constitució]] in his sole season there.<ref name="NFT"/> Martínez spent the next three years with [[FC Santa Coloma]].<ref name="NFT"/>

After winning the league title in every season with FC Santa Coloma, Martínez was signed by fellow [[Football in Andorra#League system|top-flight]] team [[Inter Club d'Escaldes|Inter d'Escaldes]] in 2017.<ref name="NFT"/> Six matches and one goal followed.<ref name="NFT"/> Martínez returned to FC Andorra in 2018, with the club now in [[Primera Catalana]].<ref name="NFT"/> In mid-2019, Martínez returned to Andorra with [[FC Ordino]].<ref name="BDF1">{{cite news|title=Joel Martínez|url=https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/c/jugador.html?id=9728|accessdate=27 August 2020|work=BDFutbol}}</ref> He appeared fifteen times in [[2019–20 Primera Divisió|2019–20]] as they suffered relegation.<ref name="BDF1"/>

While still an active player for FC Ordino, in June 2019, [[Inter Club d'Escaldes|Inter d'Escaldes]] confirmed that Martínez, who had previously also been a youth coach at the club, had been hired as coordinator of the club's football school.<ref>[https://interescaldes.com/2019/06/12/tot-queda-a-casa/#more-3451 Tot queda a casa], interescaldes.com, 12 June 2019</ref> As of June 2024, Martínez still held this role.<ref>[https://whoopcoaching.com/coaching-esportiu-amb-equip-juvenil-inter-club-escaldes/ Coaching esportiu amb l’equip juvenil de l’Inter Club Escaldes], whoopcoaching.com, 4 June 2024</ref>

==International career==
Martínez was called up by [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]] in 2007.<ref name="Soccerway"/><ref name="NFT"/> He made his debut on 28 March during a [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|UEFA Euro 2008 qualifier]] with [[England national football team|England]], with his nation losing 0–3 at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys]]; he was subbed on for [[Manolo Jiménez Soria]] after sixty-nine minutes.<ref name="BBC Sport">{{cite news|title=Andorra 0-3 England|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/internationals/6497817.stm|accessdate=14 December 2018|work=BBC Sport|date=28 March 2007}}</ref><ref name="UEFA">{{cite news|title=Gerrard spares England's blushes|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b9fe3115f-6ea22bdf283b-1000--gerrard-spares-england-s-blushes/|access-date=14 December 2018|work=UEFA|date=29 March 2007}}</ref>
